texts.descend: Lower the open jaws straight down beside the object. Use it right after approach when the object is in the opening right of the fixed jaw, even if the bottom edge cuts it off; the position gets checked and corrected once the jaws are down.
texts.nudge_right: Move the jaws toward image right. Use this only when the object is already right of the fixed jaw but too far from it, or when the fixed jaw is over another item; never when the object is left of the fixed jaw.
texts.nudge_left: Move the jaws toward image left. Use this when the object is left of the fixed jaw or under it; it carries the fixed jaw past the object so the object ends up in the opening to the jaw's right.
texts.close: Close the jaws on the object. Only do this when the object sits alongside the fixed jaw's right side, level with or below its tip, even if it fills the picture. If close just closed on nothing, don't close again: run find_object.
texts.open: Open the jaws and let go: to set the held object down, after lift shows the jaws missed the object, or when the gripper is jammed with both jaws in view and nothing held. If close stopped part way on something, lift to check before opening.
texts.nudge_in: Move the jaws a little toward the base (toward image down). Only while the jaws are still high, when the bottom edge of the picture cuts the object off; once line_up has put the object in the opening, don't nudge_in, because a cut-off bottom edge is fine there.
texts.raise: Raise the open jaws straight up, only when they are down low around the object and it is not in the opening right of the fixed jaw. If raise just stopped as blocked, do not run it again; use find_object instead.
texts.line_up: Ask Claude to move the open jaws sideways or out a little until the object sits in the opening right of the fixed jaw. It never lowers the jaws: once the object touches or nearly touches the fixed jaw's right side with its middle level with the tip, use descend instead.
texts.approach: Open the jaws and move them above the object, pointing steeply down just to its left. Run it once find_object has located the object, even if the object is not in the current picture; if approach just failed as out of reach while the object looks near, run find_object again.
